result.rationale: TopicEmbed.import interpolates url directly into HTML: `#{url}`, with only `url =~ /^https?\/\//` validation, which permits quotes and angle brackets (e.g. `http://x/' onclick='...`). The post is created with cook_method raw_html (Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]), so cook returns raw unchanged, and best.html.erb renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. No escaping step exists anywhere in the shown pipeline, so attribute breakout/HTML injection into the topic and embedded iframe is real and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the unescaped `url` is interpolated directly into an HTML attribute and element text: `"#{url}"` (within `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)`). The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes/`>` etc. The post is then created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html`, and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This makes crafted feed URLs capable of injecting arbitrary markup/JS into stored content and the embed output.
